description: Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza and Jack Bech are surging, while Khalil Shakir and Justice Hill provide immediate
body:
Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza and Jack Bech are surging, while Khalil Shakir and Justice Hill provide immediate lineup depth for managers making a playoff push
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Week 11 of the NFL season brought another important weekend of Fantasy football action, with superstar performances, unexpected breakouts and plenty of developments that could shake up the fantasy landscape heading into the final stretch of the regular season. For your fantasy leagues, you're thinking about a playoff push and possibly even what to do with your rosters heading into your league's trade deadline. Whether it was established fantasy stars continuing to deliver, unexpected players stepping up in big spots or highly drafted players struggling to meet expectations, Week 11 provided plenty of talking points. From quarterback explosions and running backs finding the end zone to wide receivers dominating target share and tight ends emerging as reliable options, there were plenty of performances worth examining.Beyond the box scores, injuries and changing offensive roles could prove just as important as the biggest fantasy performances this weekend. Several key developments could impact lineup decisions, waiver-wire priorities, and player values heading into Week 12, making it critical for fantasy managers to stay ahead of the latest news. We'll break down the biggest Week 11 fantasy performances, highlight the players whose stock is rising or falling, examine the most important injury situations, and identify potential waiver-wire additions who could make an immediate impact. With the fantasy playoffs quickly approaching, we'll also look ahead to the Week 12 matchups, identifying favorable opportunities, potential sleepers, and players managers should target as they make their final push toward the postseason.Let's take a look at several standouts from Week 11 that should be on your waiver wire radar for Week 12.Early waiver wire adds for Week 12Jonah Coleman, RB, BroncosYou can't add Coleman off waivers, but that doesn't mean you can't trade for him now prior to your trade deadline. For three weeks now, both Jacob Gibbs and I have been screaming from the rooftops to trade for Coleman. He is the definition of a buy high, now, after his breakout in Week 11. Coleman scored three touchdowns, touched the football 28 times and totaled over 100 yards. And I'm here to say you should still be looking to trade for him now. Buy high on Coleman. He projects as a top-10 play at the position in every coming game on the Broncos' schedule. 
Fernando Mendoza, QB, RaidersThere was something in the air that night, the stars to bright, Fernando! I've been waiting to type that out and thought it might take a few weeks or months before Mendoza jumped onto the Fantasy radar. It took just two starts at the NFL level. Mendoza racked up 267 passing yards and three passing touchdowns against one of the best defenses in football (Denver). He also added 22 yards rushing. That's the type of game that jolts him squarely onto the Fantasy radar. Jack Bech, WR, RaidersSpeaking of Mendoza, he's got himself a new favorite target in the pass game -- second-year mid-round draft pick Jack Bech. It's good to see Bech finally getting the opportunity to showcase his abilities after the catch and at the catch point. His rapport with Mendoza is obvious and it's important to chase rapport in Fantasy. Bech had nine targets and turned them into an uber-efficient eight catches for 88 yards and a touchdown. He is not only in the WR3 but back-end WR2 discussion moving forward, given the state of WR in Fantasy right now. Justice Hill, RB, RavensHill continues to see his role grow because he has provided a spark for the Ravens offense as a perfect complement to Derrick Henry and a change of pace. While Henry cleared concussion protocol after the game, Hill should maintain his role rest of season. That role led to 96 yards of total offense and a touchdown in Week 11. He's worth adding in PPR leagues. 
Khalil Shakir, WR, BillsShakir topped the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 11 with five receptions on nine targets. His role has continued to expand in the second half of the season and he could make for a nice FLEX play the rest of the way.

title: Fantasy Baseball: Does Tarik Skubal's record-setting contract with the Mets make him SP1? - CBS Sports
description: Or will the Mets' aggressive spending come back to bite them again?
body:
Or will the Mets' aggressive spending come back to bite them again?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Two years ago, the Mets locked up the best hitter on the free agent market with a record-setting deal. Now, they've done the same for the best pitcher, agreeing to a nine-year, $450 million contract with Tarik Skubal on Sunday. It's the biggest contract ever awarded to a pitcher, bettering the $325 million deal that the Dodgers gave Yoshinobu Yamamoto prior to the 2024 season. From a real baseball perspective, then, it's an earth-shaking development, the kind that can reshape a franchise and change the complexion of the entire league. But from a Fantasy Baseball perspective, it's ... whatever. That's generally how it works for the biggest free agents. Studs are studs no matter where they go. The fringies are the ones most impacted by their environment, to the point it can make or break them, even. Skubal, however, is such a perfect pitcher -- rating among the best in strikeouts, walks and contact quality -- that the depth of the fence or the proficiency of the defense isn't going to have a dramatic effect on his performance. We already got a glimpse of that in 2026, when he was traded from the Tigers, a bad team in a pitcher's park, to the Dodgers, a good team in a hitter's park. His production was almost exactly the same. I may be overstating the tendency of both of those venues a little, but the fact is that Citi Field is considered the most "neutral" of the three, if that's such a thing.  

    
                 
                        LAD

On good teams or bad, in one park or another, Skubal has been Cy Young-caliber for three consecutive seasons, winning the award in both 2024 and 2025. You may think the Mets are the Wile E. Coyote of baseball teams, having their sleek ACME rocket blow up on the launching pad time and time again, but if midseason elbow surgery in 2026 wasn't enough to bring Skubal down, I'm thinking he'll be OK here as well. Of course, sometimes free agents flop for other reasons, and a deal such as this one does subject Skubal to the pressure of living up to it while under the scrutiny of the New York media. We've seen other big-dollar free agents struggle under similar circumstances before regaining their footing in Year 2, so it can happen. But matters of psychology aren't really my domain -- nor are they yours, unless you've treated Skubal. Any claims of this deal being his downfall, while distinctly possible due to the nature of pitching, are unwarranted doomerism. Bottom line is that I have every reason to believe Skubal will be in the running for a Cy Young again, and while he wasn't quite as good in 2026 as the eventual Cy Young winners, Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler, he's arguably the safest pick of the three for 2027, having performed at that level not just once but three times in a row. He's already proven he can bounce back from the big workload they just took on for the first time, and while he throws plenty hard himself, he doesn't max out the radar gun quite like they do. That second point is especially pertinent in the case of Misiorowski, who is so far the only starting pitcher going ahead of Skubal by ADP. He's the latest to claim the mantle of "hardest-throwing starting pitcher in history," and let's just say his predecessors haven't stood out for their longevity. So does Skubal have a case to be the top starting pitcher drafted in Fantasy? Yes, but that was always the case. The headline was a clickbaity way to imply that the Mets had something to do with it. Gotcha! 
Thank you, as always, for reading.

title: Vikings utilize NFL's obscure fair-catch kick rule to attempt 71-yard field goal against 49ers - CBS Sports
description: If made, Will Reichard's field goal would have made NFL history
body:
If made, Will Reichard's field goal would have made NFL history
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The game between the Vikings and the 49ers got a little confusing toward the end of the first half on Sunday night when Minnesota decided to take advantage of an obscure NFL rule known as the fair-catch kick. With 11 seconds left to play in the first half, the 49ers were facing a fourth-and-19 from their own 11-yard line, which was an obvious punting situation for San Francisco. Vikings returner Myles Price called for a fair catch on the play, and that's where the rarely used fair-catch kick came in. Basically, the rule goes like this: If a team fair catches a punt, they're allowed to attempt a free kick on the next play. The kick isn't a typical field goal, either. The defense has to line up 10 yards off the ball — similar to a kickoff — and the defense is NOT allowed to try to block the kick. The "free kick" is more like a kickoff, except the kicker has to attempt the field goal off the ground, and there's also a holder (the kicker also has the option to dropkick the ball, but that almost never happens). Here's how the NFL describes the rule: "After a fair catch, the receiving team has the option to put the ball in play by a snap or a fair-catch kick (field goal attempt), with fair-catch kick lines established ten yards apart. All general rules apply as for a field goal attempt from scrimmage. The clock starts when the ball is kicked. (No tee permitted.)"
History nearly made in Mexico CityNow that you know how the rule works, let's get back to the game. Price actually called for a fair catch from his own 40-yard line, which meant that if the Vikings wanted to take advantage of the rule, they would have to attempt a 71-YARD FIELD GOAL. With the game being played in Mexico City, which sits at an elevation of 7,350 feet, that adds about five yards to a kicker's natural distance, so the Vikings decided to send out Will Reichard for the potentially record-setting kick. According to the broadcast, Reichard hit from 68 yards in warm-ups, so the Vikings thought he could hit from 71, and it ALMOST HAPPENED. Reichard's kick only fell about a yard short. 
If the kick had gone in, it would have counted in the record book as the longest field goal in NFL history. But since he missed, Cam Little still holds the record at 68 yards. There have only been 10 field goal attempts ever from 70 yards or longer, and Little actually had one of them back in Week 3 when he just barely missed a kick against the Patriots. Out of the other nine attempts, four of them came on a fair-catch kick, including Reichards'.
The fair-catch kick is rare: There have only been 21 attempts ever in the Super Bowl era, and only one kicker has actually made one over the past 40 years (Cameron Dicker in December 2024). Reichard had a chance at NFL history on Sunday night, but he came up about a yard short. Reichard also missed a 55-yard attempt in the first half.

title: Victor Wembanyama takes hypocritical jab at 'stat-padding peers' after hunting his own 50-piece - CBS Sports
description: Wembanyama is just as guilty of the basketball crimes he loves to rail against, but that's not stopping him from
body:
Wembanyama is just as guilty of the basketball crimes he loves to rail against, but that's not stopping him from getting on his soapbox
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words. Stephen Curry is the only player I can remember thinking of the same way in the post-Michael Jordan era. Nobody else. With Steph and Wemby, you can't fully describe what you've seen. You try, but in the end you just have to see them to understand. It's totally different than anything you've ever witnessed on a basketball court. So here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday. It feels like we're qualifying one of his "first in history" stat lines about once a week, and indeed, Wembanyama is the first player since blocks and steals became an official stat in 1973 to record those single-game numbers. Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children. 
Before the halftime buzzer had even sounded, Wembanyama had already tallied 32 points, 13 rebounds, three steals and three blocks. That would be a career game for a lot of NBA players. He had played 18 minutes. You can only laugh at this point.
What was even funnier, however, was Wembanyama's comment after the game, when he took a clear stab at, well, whoever he considers his "peers" to be by calling them out for, shall we say, unethical statistical pursuits. "It is very special," Wembanyama said of reaching the 50-point mark for the second time this season and third time in his career. "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not good at stat-padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have."
So here's what's interesting about this little dig: Wembanyama was definitely guilty of stat-padding his way to 50 in this game. With just more than eight minutes remaining and the Spurs up by 24, Wembanyama could've stayed on the bench after the timeout. The Spurs have made a concerted effort to limit his minutes whenever possible this year. Even in the golden age of comebacks, this game was over. 
But Wemby stayed in and proceeded to take five straight shots on the next five possessions. He was hunting the 50. No question about it. He even admitted as much. "The greats of the game, they don't care [about stat-padding]," Wemby said, via The Athletic. "I don't think Wilt [Chamberlain] thought about that when he had 98 points. ... That stepback 3, going right, that I took, it doesn't correlate with this. It didn't fit to the definition [of ethical basketball], for example. So I did try [to stat-pad] at the end."Good on Wemby for acknowledging his own hypocrisy, but it raises the question: if you just did the very thing you are railing against, why take the jab in the first place? Every player who has been within range of 50 points has gone for it as long as it's not a competitive game in which quality shots still matter. It's not that big a deal.
But Wemby has done this before. In December of 2025, after the Spurs had just defeated the Thunder, he said, "I'm just glad to be part of something that's growing to be so beautiful — pure and ethical basketball."This was a definite jab at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-baiting. Wemby, meanwhile, has turned into one of the more theatrical floppers in the league. In almost every way, Wembanyama is different than any other basketball player in the world. But when it comes to this ethical, non-stat-padding basketball soapbox he has climbed upon on numerous occasions, the truth is he's just like everyone else. So enough with the jabs.

body:
Travis Etienne seizes the Saints backfield, Rashee Rice slips out of must-start territory and more early-slate trade and waiver takeaways as the fantasy playoffs approach
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026

    9:34 pm ET

        The Fantasy football season is reaching the stretch run and now is crunch time. It's likely your trade deadline is approaching fast in most leagues, and now is your chance to strike on some of the best buy-low and buy-high trade candidates. Week 11 brought us plenty of action in the early slate of games and now comes the fallout. Let's take a look at the most important takeaways from the early-slate action and how you should approach these developments from a Fantasy football standpoint.Here are some Fantasy thoughts from Sunday's early games: Kansas City 34 – Arizona 7NOT A WINNER BUT NOT A LOSER: Trey McBrideYou love 14 targets, but you hate 54 yards. Obviously, the Cardinals' offense is a mess and won't score many touchdowns going forward. I assume Carson Beck will be the starter when healthy, and I don't think that's good for McBride. On the bright side, the schedule will get a lot easier. I think McBride will be fine, but not a league winner.LOSER: Rashee RiceRice is simply not running enough routes. Unofficially, he ran about 60% of the routes with Patrick Mahomes on the field and hasn't reached a 70% route participation rate since returning from injury in Week 8. And with Josh Downs commanding targets (and still working his way into a bigger route participation rate), Rice is no longer a must-start player. I still anticipate him being a Top 24 WR for the rest of the season, but I'm not expecting him to be anywhere near as consistent as we drafted him to be. Dallas 51 – Tennessee 30NOT AS GOOD AS THE NUMBERS: Cam WardWard scored 26.2 Fantasy points (6 point per passing TD) but got very lucky with a fluky 59-yard TD throw to Carnell Tate and a wacky across-his-body TD throw to Calvin Ridley in garbage time. He did not move the ball effectively against the Cowboys, and I won't be trusting him next week against the Jaguars. He could be an OK contributor later in the year as the schedule gets very favorable. 
Philadelphia 19 – Pittsburgh 16ENCOURAGED: DeVonta SmithSmith had 12 targets on 21 pass attempts from Joe Milton. He turned those 12 targets into 41 yards, but he and Milton were close to connecting on a few chunk plays. Of course, Milton is not an accurate QB, and that will hold Smith back, but it was nice to see him as the focal point of the passing game. He's a low-end WR2 going forward. DISCOURAGED: Jaylen WarrenTwo duds in a row for Warren (at Cincinnati and at Philadelphia). It's a fairly even split with Rico Dowdle, though Warren still appears to be the lead back for the Steelers. Overall, I just don't have much faith in the Steelers' offense. I will continue to start Warren, but I'm a little nervous about it. Buffalo 26 – Miami 9ENCOURAGED #1: DJ Moore scored 23.1 PPR Fantasy points, the most by any WR against the Dolphins this season. He looked great all game. I really hate his schedule going forward, so I wouldn't mind trying to sell high on Moore (if your trade deadline hasn't passed). But you've got to get him something great. 
ENCOURAGED #2: Caleb DouglasSimilar to DeVonta Smith, Douglas was close to big production today. He dropped a pass around in the five-yard line that likely would have been a TD had he been able to make the catch. Douglas has 18 targets in his last two games, so he is clearly the top option in this passing game. You can still consider him a WR3. Chicago 21 – New Orleans 13DUD OF THE WEEK: Jordyn TysonI was excited to start Tyson this week, and boy was I wrong to be excited. Tyson was started in 62% of CBS leagues and he rewarded his Fantasy managers with one catch for six yards on two targets. Unofficially, he ran fewer than 50% of the routes. Where do we go from here? I still think he's a WR3 and I'm definitely not dropping him. There will be better days ahead. WINNER: Travis EtienneEtienne dominated carries and looks like the clear RB1 in the Saints backfield. He'll be a starting option for Fantasy managers now, though probably not a great one. 
Detroit 31 – Tampa Bay 21NOT BUYING IT: Ted HurstHurst led the Bucs in every receiving category, but I'm not adding him outside of very deep leagues. SIT HIM: Emeka EgbukaEgbuka was started in 65% of leagues, and that makes sense with six teams on a bye. And let's give credit to the Lions defense, which has improved throughout the season, but how can we trust Egbuka at this point? I'm not saying he's a must-sit, but I hope you have better options. He's in the same category as Caleb Douglas and Jordyn Tyson. Carolina 35 – Baltimore 33I'M CONFUSED: Bryce YoungI don't feel confident knowing when to start or sit Young. His next two games are at Tampa Bay and at Minnesota, so I'm going to sit him. I think I'm actually going to be right! Keep an eye on injuries in the Bucs secondary before making that decision in Week 12. 
WORTH A LOOK: Justice HillI know Hill had a good day as a rusher (and nearly a great day, but he fumbled just before reaching the goal line), but it's his receiving role that makes him a potential flex in PPR leagues. Hill has three or more catches in six straight games, and the Ravens might be a pass-heavy team with Jacoby Brissett.

title: Justin Herbert in concussion protocol after loss to Jets: Chargers QB played entire game - CBS Sports
description: Herbert took some big shots late in the game but did not exit
body:
Herbert took some big shots late in the game but did not exit
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Justin Herbert is in the NFL's concussion protocol after the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets, per the team. It's unclear when Herbert suffered the injury, as he played the whole game, but concussion-like symptoms can appear well after the collisions that cause the concussions themselves.Because he entered concussion protocol, Herbert did not address the media after the game.Herbert went 15-for-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 32 yards and a score as well. He took six sacks, though, and has now taken an NFL-high 39 sacks this season.
Herbert has been an ironman, especially considering the hits he has taken in his career behind a seemingly ever-shaky offensive line. Only one injury has forced Herbert to miss a game in his career: A fractured finger on his throwing hand required surgery and cost him the final four contests of the 2023 campaign.
The Chargers (1-9) have had a miserable season, with the much-hyped pairing of Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel failing to mesh. Herbert has thrown just eight touchdown passes compared to 11 interceptions and is on pace for career worsts nearly across the board. He had played his first two turnover-free games of the season — last week in a win over the Ravens and Sunday against New York — but now could miss time depending on how concussion protocol progresses.
If entering the protocol does force Herbert to miss time, the Chargers would turn to DJ Uiagalelei. He has played in one NFL game, in mop-up duty against the Texans in Week 9. He went 2-for-7 for 24 yards and a touchdown. Los Angeles also has Jake Browning on the practice squad.

title: NFL Week 11 winners and losers: Cowboys offense makes history in get-right win, Steelers slump - CBS Sports
description: Dallas scored on all but one possession in a bounce-back victory, while Pittsburgh's postseason hopes took a hit
body:
Dallas scored on all but one possession in a bounce-back victory, while Pittsburgh's postseason hopes took a hit
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Dallas Cowboys have to light up the scoreboard to win games in 2026, and they did just that in Week 11. The superstars on their offense showed up emphatically in a "gotta have it" kind of game against the Tennessee Titans and, for at least one week, deflected some of the deserved scrutiny that has been trained on the defense all season.Dallas, therefore, is among the biggest winners of the week across the NFL this week. Sunday's schedule was one where heavy favorites had little to gain but everything to lose, and to the Cowboys' credit, they not only avoided disaster but also took care of business in emphatic fashion. They were not the only team to do so, but they needed that kind of win more than any of the other franchises that entered the week on the right side of a lopsided point spread.But at the same time, the Pittsburgh Steelers were among the teams to feel the sting of failing to live up to expectations against a beleaguered opponent.Here are the greatest winners and losers from Sunday's Week 11 action.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Cowboys offenseThe defense is still an issue even after Christian Parker's demotion from play-caller, as evidenced by the 30 points it surrendered to the lowly Titans and the breakdown that allowed Carnell Tate to score one of the strangest touchdowns of the year. But when a team can score at will, what happens on the other side of the ball hardly matters. That was the case for the Cowboys in a 51-30 drubbing of the Titans.
Dallas needed a win in this spot, and they got it in the worst way. A season that is already slipping through its fingers would have only gotten more depressing with a loss to a one-win team. Behind a nearly perfect game from Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Javonte Williams and the rest of the offense, the Cowboys avoided disaster by a healthy margin and notched their third win in five games, keeping them very much alive in the NFC East race.The Cowboys scored on all of their possessions except the final one when they knelt out the clock. They found the end zone seven times and scored a touchdown on each of their first six drives, the franchise's longest run of consecutive possessions ending in a touchdown to open a game in the play-by-play era. Some of that success had to do with the Titans' bleak defensive situation—their 13 straight drives with points allowed dating back to Week 10 were the most in a single season since at least 2000, per NFL research—but just as much with the star power on their own offense.In the process, Lamb became the first receiver in Cowboys history with six consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. He and Pickens both crossed the 100-yard mark in the blowout.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: SteelersThe last time the Steelers beat the Philadelphia Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love? 1965. Granted, as members of opposite conferences, the in-state rivals only play every few years. But this is a losing streak that now spans 12 games after Sunday's 19-16 result, which went in favor of the Eagles.This was the kind of matchup that was supposed to help the Steelers bounce back from last week's no-show against the Cincinnati Bengals and work their way back toward the top of the AFC North. Instead, they lost to a team that hadn't won a game since September and started Joe Milton at quarterback. It is far too early to call it a devastating loss, but if the Steelers finish the season a game short of a playoff berth, it is a contest they will look back on as one they should have gotten.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Panthers' NFC South outlookThe Carolina Panthers survived a shootout with the Baltimore Ravens that stands competitively among the most entertaining and chaotic games of the season. There were seven lead changes in the contest, including four in a back-and-forth second quarter and two in the final period. The Panthers were responsible for that final go-ahead play: A 37-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald with 1:44 to play. The kick put the NFC South leaders up 35-33.
On a day when every other team in the division either lost or was on a bye, the Panthers capitalized on their opportunity to distance themselves from the pack. They now stand two games clear of the three other squads, all with 3-7 records.A loss would not have cost Carolina its division lead, but it would have been a difficult pill to swallow, given the Ravens hadn't even led in a game since Oct. 25, before the multiple advantages they held on Sunday. But by taking care of business at home against the reeling Ravens, Carolina improved to .500 on the year and is now looking like a more respectable division leader.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Trevor LawrenceHigh yardage total aside, Trevor Lawrence had a day to forget. His 301 passing yards were more a product of the large passing volume required of him in a loss than anything else. The New York Giants defense had him pressing in a 23-18 loss and forced him into a number of errors including two interceptions, a pick on a 2-point attempt, three sacks and a whopping 22 incompletions.
Rarely have the Jacksonville Jaguars found themselves in negative game scripts this season. Lawrence was fantastic in one of them (when he threw four touchdowns in a loss to the Houston Texans) but struggled in two others.It took until the fourth quarter for Lawrence to lead the Jaguars to a touchdown, but by that point, it was too late. The Giants had already done enough damage in building a 14-point lead. Jacksonville needed Lawrence's typical MVP-caliber passing ability to shine in order to pull off the comeback but did not get it. And as a result, they are behind pace in the battle for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Travis KelceThis deep into such a lengthy and legendary career, Travis Kelce routinely reaches landmarks on team and league leaderboards. Sunday was another historic day for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end. Kelce scored two touchdowns in the 34-7 rout of the Arizona Cardinals and thus hauled in multiple scoring passes for the first time in 47 games. Ending that prolonged drought also moved Kelce up a spot on the NFL tight end career touchdown list.
Most total touchdowns by tight end (regular season and playoffs)Antonio Gates (118)Tony Gonzalez (115)Travis Kelce (110)Rob Gronkowski (109)What better day to make history than the same day on which Kelce became the fourth player in Chiefs history to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead Stadium? That is some serious longevity.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: DK MetcalfAs if the loss to the Eagles was not bad enough for DK Metcalf and the Steelers, the wide receiver made his day even worse with an inexcusable decision. Metcalf had been jawing at Philadelphia defenders all game and took it to another level when he poked Cooper DeJean in the eye a little more than halfway through the third quarter. That exchange drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty (Metcalf's second of the game) and prompted his ejection from the game.
Metcalf did not back up his trash talk with his performance. He caught just one pass for 2 yards across four targets.
The NFL fined Metcalf earlier this season for taunting in the Steelers' Week 4 loss to the Browns. He also served a two-game suspension last season for getting into a physical altercation with a fan.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Bears GM Ryan PolesThe Chicago Bears' trade deadline blockbuster continues to age to perfection. Jeffery Simmons has been nothing but a superstar since his arrival in the Windy City and turned in his best performance as a Bear in the 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints. Simmons racked up three sacks for the second time in his career, also recording three tackles for loss in a game for the fourth time. He led a vicious pass rush that got home on Tyler Shough six times.Each of general manager Ryan Poles' moves ahead of and during the season contributed to where the Bears stand as a contender for the NFC's No. 1 seed. The Simmons trade is the latest and most stupendous example, but Poles made several other transactions that have been just as impactful. The Garrett Bradbury trade added a reliable starter to the middle of the offensive line, and sending DJ Moore out of town for two draft picks opened the door for Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze to flourish as a prolific receiving tandem.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Chargers' quest for a win streakIt is a good thing for the Los Angeles Chargers that they finally ended their winless season last week, because if Sunday's showing is any indication of what is to come over the final month of the season, one win is all they might end up with. A home game against the reeling New York Jets is about as winnable of an opportunity as there is in the NFL in 2026, but the Chargers could not take advantage. They dropped to 1-9 on the year with the 27-24 loss.Making matters worse, Justin Herbert is now in concussion protocol. DJ Uiagalelei is the No. 2 quarterback and has never started a game.This was a chance for Los Angeles to begin stacking wins and make this disaster of a season look a little less devastating. There is some runway ahead with games against the Drake Maye-less New England Patriots, the sub-.500 Tampa Bay Buccaneers and a Las Vegas Raiders team starting a rookie quarterback. Had the Chargers gotten the job done against the Jets, they could have legitimately sparked a hot streak. But following the loss and with Herbert's status in question, they might just slip deeper into a hole.
Winner: Home teamsEntering Sunday, the last time home teams went undefeated in the early window was back in Week 9 of the 2019 season. It was therefore a rare sight to see the Panthers, Eagles, Chiefs, Cowboys, Bears, Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills all defend home turf during the 1 p.m. ET slate.Including the Texans on "Thursday Night Football," home teams opened the week at 8-0.The Broncos and Giants added to the ledger in the late window, while the Chargers were the only home squad to fall. The final tally heading into the Sunday night game was 10-1.

title: Dwight Howard admits he told Magic not to trade for Stephen Curry before he became 'one of the greatest' - CBS Sports
description: Howard said his priority at the time was getting Monta Ellis to Orlando
body:
Howard said his priority at the time was getting Monta Ellis to Orlando
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history. There were never serious rumors, for instance, about LeBron James or Michael Jordan getting traded. Magic Johnson and Kobe Bryant both issued public trade demands, but pulled back before a deal was consummated. Players like this, for the most part, don't make it to the rumor mill because nobody ever thinks they're seriously available.The exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry. Though the rumors all died once he hit his prime, there is a rich history of teams that nearly traded for the greatest shooter of all time before he became, well, the greatest shooter of all time. At least three notable deals were reportedly scuttled at the finish line:On the night of the 2009 NBA Draft, Curry was almost traded for Phoenix Suns star Amar'e Stoudemire. The Suns at the time were run by current Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr. Curry's father, current Hornets broadcaster and former NBA player Dell Curry, later revealed that Kerr called him asking not to take Curry to his press conference after getting drafted. "We have a trade that they reneged on," Curry says Kerr said at the time. He did go through with that press conference, and Kerr would eventually get to work with Curry in Golden State instead of Phoenix.Curry and Klay Thompson were almost traded to the New Orleans Hornets for Chris Paul in 2011, Ethan Sherwood Strauss reported in his book "The Victory Machine." Paul, in an interview with UNINTERRUPTED, explained that he told the Warriors that he would not sign an extension with the Warriors.One of the foundational moves of Golden State's ascent was its decision to trade its other explosive scoring guard, Monta Ellis, for Andrew Bogut in part to seemingly hand the reins of the offense to Curry in 2012. The only problem? Several stakeholders have attested that Curry, not Ellis, was originally meant to be in that trade. "That was the deal," former Bucks owner Marc Lasry told The Athletic in 2019. "But the Bucks' medical staff didn't think Steph's ankle would hold up. That killed the deal." Bogut himself backed up this assertion in an interview on the House of Strauss podcast, saying Milwaukee's medical team told him as much. "I had a good relationship with them, so they just blatantly told me: 'The other option was Steph and his bad ankle. We decided to go with Monta.' So I was like, 'Alright.'"There have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries. Of course, Curry differs from those contemporaries in one key way: he was not a sure thing. James came into the NBA as a preordained star. Anyone claiming they knew what Curry was going to become is almost certainly lying. There was quite a bit of doubt about him early in his career, and that doubt informs our latest entry into the Curry trade chronicles.Dwight Howard appeared on the AM Hoops Show on Saturday and shared something few would be eager to admit: he told his former team, the Orlando Magic, not to trade for Stephen Curry. "I wanted to play with Monta Ellis and the Magic wanted to get Steph. The Magic wanted to get Steph and I said no. I said no because I didn't know. I didn't know Steph Curry was going to be one of the greatest," Howard said, regretfully. Asked specifically if the Magic came to him with this, he confirmed. "At the time, Monta was the one who was playing all the minutes," he added.
Howard did not offer a specific trade proposal or window of time when this could have happened, but two options come to mind. The first would be during the 2010-11 season, when Orlando revamped its team in mid-December by making two blockbuster deals that sent Vince Carter, Rashard Lewis, Marcin Gortat and Mickael Pietrus out while bringing back Gilbert Arenas, Hedo Turkoglu, Jason Richardson and Earl Clark. This would make sense as a period of roster transition, and Ellis was the league leader in minutes that season, averaging more than 40 per game across 80 appearances.But Curry was no slouch that season when it came to availability either. He appeared in 74 games and averaged nearly 34 minutes. His availability didn't become a major concern until a year later, when ankle injuries limited him to just 26 games. At that point, his trade value would have been at its lowest, and Howard's leverage with the team would have been at its height. Howard had a player option for the 2012-13 season that he surprisingly exercised... even though the Magic didn't acquire Ellis. Orlando still wound up trading Howard to the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2012.On paper, Curry was perhaps the perfect guard to pair with Howard at his peak. Of course, Curry was and remains the perfect player to pair with just about anyone, but Howard, specifically, tried and failed to mesh with two high-usage star guards in Kobe Bryant and James Harden. Curry's eagerness to play off of the ball would have allowed Howard more post-up possessions, a priority of his at the time even if such plays didn't represent great offense. The team could have run through Howard, but still benefitted enormously from the young Curry's presence before eventually shifting in Curry's direction as Howard aged out of his physical prime. 
Stan Van Gundy was a pioneer in the 3-point revolution, building a four-out lineup around Howard with players like Lewis and Turkoglu. It's tempting to think about what he could have done with a young Curry, especially since Van Gundy would miss another chance to coach him down the line, when he elected to take the Detroit Pistons job in 2014 rather than continuing to pursue Golden State's vacant position.But if there ever really was a window for someone to swoop in and steal Curry, it closed after that third, injury-plagued season. Curry broke out in the 2012-13 season by leading the Warriors back to the playoffs, made his first All-Star team a year later, and then a year after that, he won the first of his two MVP awards and four championships. From that point forward, Golden State had no reason to ever entertain the notion of trading Curry, and Howard, like the Suns, Hornets and Bucks, was left to wonder about what might have been.Ironically enough, Howard would get another chance to pair up with Curry in 2013, after Curry had proven himself as Golden State's lead guard. He was a free agent that offseason and met with the Warriors, but seemingly preferred Harden as his running mate, as he signed with the Houston Rockets. The Warriors turned around and used their cap flexibility to add dynasty mainstay Andre Iguodala, an essential part of a team that largely won without high-profile centers like Howard. With the benefit of hindsight, Howard might be one of the most important hidden figures in Golden State's rise to prominence. If he had any inkling of the sort of legend Curry was destined to become, the Warriors dynasty may never have happened.

title: Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky - CBS Sports
description: The two-time Cy Young winner and best available free agent has landed a nine-year, $450 million contract with the
body:
The two-time Cy Young winner and best available free agent has landed a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The big prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal. The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team. Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the Mets are getting a surefire ace for nearly a decade. Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.
Track record, including workloadSince returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.The recent track record here says this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close). There isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings. 
He's stellar. Pretty much all the time. Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season. There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.Age and injury historyWe'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026. The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level. 
Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings. Pitchers age well nowadaysI mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory. Verlander won a Cy Young at age 36 and then again at age 39. Max Scherzer finished third in Cy Young voting at age 36 and was still very good at age 37 (5.3 WAR, 2.29 ERA in 23 starts).Chris Sale won a Cy Young in his age-35 season and was still excellent this past season at age 37.Zack Wheeler came off thoracic outlet surgery last year at age 36 to post a 6.1 WAR in 28 starts.Jacob deGrom had a 2.97 ERA in 30 starts as a 37-year-old.Sonny Gray just went 18-5 with a 2.72 ERA in his age-36 season. Zack Greinke was still great at age 35 and pretty darn good at age 38. Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. His nine-year deal means it'll run through his age-38 season. 
For those so worried about the long-term finances of the Cohen family, are you sure you're really worried that Skubal won't be productive through five, six or even all nine years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet. Megadeals for pitchers have mostly been good recentlyA decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding). Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?
Gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.Justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times. 
Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.David Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal. Corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.
Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons. Max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.
$/WAR?We can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question: Are you sure a 9-year, $450 million deal for this guy is a "risk?" I think we could argue that it'll be a bargain.

The Tigers will move up in this week's poll, but the real question will be: will the SEC punish Will Wade's team after playing Luis? We will see. Last week: 25

The Aggies improved to 6-0 with a win over TCU on the road behind 29 points from PJ Haggerty. Texas A&M also has a win over Oklahoma State this season. Last week: NR

The free agent ace will join a rotation that includes Nolan McLean and Christian Scott
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the New York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post. The deal has a $45 million signing bonus with no options or opt-outs, per SNY, as well as a full no-trade clause, so the Mets have locked Skubal up for the full nine years. Further, there are only $30 million in deferrals, according to the New York Post. The deal is pending a physical.Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary. 
        
            
                Winners and losers of the Tarik Skubal signing: Blue Jays, Dodgers strike out; David Stearns looks nervous
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov. 20, is the No. 1 ranked talent on our list of the top 50 free agents for this offseason. Here's part of Mike Axisa's write-up: "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself."Over the last three seasons, Skubal has pitched to a 2.42 ERA and an FIP of 2.48 in 546 innings spread over 88 starts. That amounts to a total WAR of 17.7 since the start of the 2024 campaign. Skubal remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and this signing reflects that reality. Since Skubal was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the 2026 deadline, he was ineligible to receive the qualifying offer from the Dodgers. As such, the Mets will not be penalized a draft pick for signing Skubal. 
The nine years here aren't record-setting, as the longest pitcher contract remains the 12-year deal that Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers. Yamamoto's $325 million was previously the largest contract for a pitcher -- obviously excepting Shohei Ohtani, as he's a two-way player -- so Skubal's $450 million shatters that record.
        
            
                All the records broken by Tarik Skubal's nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Coming off a disappointing 88-loss campaign in 2026, the Mets, big-spending owner Steve Cohen, and lead decision-maker David Stearns needed to make an offseason splash to improve their chances of a 2027 rebound and inspire a perhaps disaffected fan base. Skubal more than qualifies. He'll front a Mets rotation that also includes 25-year-old right-hander Nolan McLean, who himself has frontline long-term potential. In Queens, Skubal joins a roster that also includes the All-Star likes of Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette. Further, the Mets just locked up young outfielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year, $95 million extension and we all know plenty about Soto's monster contract. The Mets now have Soto through 2039, Skubal through 2035, Ewing through 2034 and Lindor through 2031. 
The rotation for the Mets right now looks something like: SkubalMcLeanChristian ScottZac ThorntonSean Manaea or Kodai Senga
        
            
                What's next for the Mets after record-breaking deal with Tarik Skubal? Biggest needs for 2027
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Given the large outlay for Skubal here, the Mets should be all-in on improving the ballclub for the 2027 season, which means we shouldn't expect them to stop with just signing Skubal. That last spot in the rotation, as such, should be ticketed to someone else outside the organization at present, whether a free agent or a trade acquisition. The landing of the top free agent available no doubt ramps up the pressure on Stearns and the Mets to deliver a playoff berth and a deep October run in 2027, but Skubal's presence also makes it much likely that such a feat comes to pass.

A lockout may be coming, but nobody told the hot stove. It's already burning bright with even the biggest prize, two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, coming off the market.Once the lockout becomes official, the signings -- and all other transactions -- will cease, but those that occur before then will still count toward the date when baseball is allowed to resume. So we'd better document them all here, just like any other offseason, breaking down their impact for Fantasy Baseball.       That's what Scott White and Chris Towers intend to do over the next few weeks, at least, before everything goes quiet. They'll eventually pick up where they left off when the hot stove heats up again in ... March? Hopefully not much later than that.       Whatever the timeline, you'll want this page bookmarked so you can get the first word on everything that happens.

This is a trade that makes a ton of sense for real-life baseball but might be a disaster for Fantasy. The Mariners got -0.5 WAR from their third basemen in 2026, per FanGraphs, and Garcia represents a significant upgrade from that. As recently as 2025, put up a .286/.351/.449 line and was a borderline elite Fantasy option as a result. Unfortunately for our purposes, this trade makes it a lot less likely he'll live up to that level of play in 2027. Kauffman Stadium in Kansas City suppresses homers but is generally a pretty good offensive environment, sporting the seventh-best park factor for hitters, per BaseballSavant.com. T-Mobile Park in Seattle? It's the worst hitter's park in baseball by a pretty wide margin, though how that impacts each individual hitter often varies. Randy Arozarena more or less held serve in his time in Seattle, while someone like Eugenio Suarez struggled mightily in both stints there. It's something about the way hitters see the ball and how the humid, often chilly atmosphere affects batted balls' trajectories. There just isn't another offensive environment in baseball quite like T-Mobile Park, and it generally serves as a drag on offense across the board.   If Garcia can hit like he did in 2025, he'll still be very fantasy-relevant, however. That season saw Garcia max out his power, bumping his average exit velocity to 91.3 mph, while also increasing his launch angle, allowing him to tap into far more of that power than ever before. That he did it without sacrificing his superlative contact skills made for a very strong package. But he gave back nearly all of those improvements in 2026 and returned to being a roughly average hitter. He struggled while playing through injuries to his left hand and wrist before eventually going on the IL for nearly two months, then struggled with hamstring issues late in the season. If the injuries explain his struggles, then betting on a bounceback makes sense, even in Seattle.   
But 2025 might have just been a career year, and the move to T-Mobile Park makes it even less likely he'll get back to that level. Garcia's price has already slipped to 169.4 in early NFBC drafts, but I'd expect it to drop even farther after this. He's a fringe starting-caliber third baseman for Fantasy, and I'd take at least Curtis Mead and Isaac Paredes ahead of him, among players with a current lower ADP. --Chris Towers      Bryce Miller traded to the RoyalsWhile Maikel Garcia is going to the worst hitter's park in the league, Miller suffers from the opposite move, exiting one of the best pitching environments in the league. It's one he has specifically benefited from, sporting a career 3.49 ERA at home compared to a 4.63 ERA on the road. It would be overly simplistic to say he has lost whatever Fantasy relevance he had with this move, but it might not end up wrong.

He's had stretches across different seasons where he has looked like an ace, but he never manages to sustain it. He has pitched through various elbow issues over the years, but when he is right, he rides a high-vert, high-velo fastball to very good results. Let's not forget that he started the 2026 season with a 1.71 ERA and 10.6 K/9 in his first eight starts, but then he tried pitching through a lat issue and wasn't the same. Still, it was another reminder of how good he can be at his best. Given the inconsistency and the park downgrade, Miller should continue to see his price fall. It's not the first place I would have bet on Gray signing, but the Twins have made it clear since the most recent trade deadline that they aren't looking to rebuild. The deal is officially for one year but includes a 2028 player option for the 37-year-old Gray, meaning the Twins will either be happy about getting one great season out of him or will be looking at a fairly onerous (but short!) deal for 2028. It's a tradeoff worth making for a team like the Twins, who have talent in the rotation but little in the way of sure things, either from a performance or a health perspective. Gray is seemingly a different type of pitcher every season, but from a real-life perspective, it's easy to see the appeal in employing him: He has made at least 24 starts in every season since 2017 (minus the shortened 2020 season) and has had an ERA over 4.00 just twice in his past eight seasons. From a Fantasy perspective, his value is a little less clear. He had an excellent 2026 season that saw him take advantage of an elite Red Sox defense to put up a 2.72 ERA. It did, however, come with a huge decrease in his strikeout rate, and that came after two seasons with a combined ERA of 4.07. He's almost always a must-start pitcher, but it often feels like you can't fully trust him. Of course, with an ADP around 150 in early drafts, it doesn't really matter if you can fully trust him. Just roll him out there, hope the ERA is closer to 3.50 than 4.00 and don't overthink it. He's a 32-year-old closer, and while he has mostly been a very good one over the past six seasons, there have been enough bumps in the road along the way to make the risk for Bednar pretty obvious. But from a Fantasy perspective, Bednar safely looks like a top-12 closer now that he's returning to the Yankees. His strikeout rate regressed in 2026, but his swinging-strike rate was actually higher than the previous season, and none of his underlying metrics otherwise really tell the story of a pitcher in decline. He's somewhere shy of the elite tier of closers for Fantasy, but he's good enough (and secure enough in his role for a good team) to be worth drafting as your primary source of saves. --Chris Towers   
    Ryan Jeffers accepts Twins' qualifying offer   It was a mild surprise to see the Twins extend Jeffers the qualifying offer, but it's not a surprise to see him accept it. Jeffers is a solid starting catcher -- good enough to be worth a fair share of playing time from the DH spot but he isn't the kind of player who was likely looking at a bunch of $50-plus million offers either. It's why taking the $23.2 million qualifying offer (and becoming the highest-paid catcher in baseball by annual value!) makes some sense here.

He's a nice rotation filler for the White Sox, but unless something drastic happens to change his profile, he's a better source of GIFs than Fantasy production at this point in his career. --Chris Towers

title: Cam Skattebo flips: Giants RB celebrates game-clinching drive with backflip days after retiring it - CBS Sports
description: Skattebo said he'd retire his celebration in the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
body:
Skattebo said he'd retire his celebration in the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After Lions star Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL going airborne while celebrating a sack in Week 10, Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he'd retire his signature backflip celebration.It proved a very short retirement.Skattebo delivered the game-clinching first down in the Giants' 23-18 upset win over the Jaguars and celebrated ... with a backflip.
It was a huge win for the Giants, who moved to 6-3-1 to remain two games up on the Cowboys (5-6) in the NFC East. Dallas won earlier Sunday.It was also a huge sigh of relief for Skattebo, who had a crucial fumble that contributed to Jacksonville's late rally. Overall, Skattebo finished with 14 carries for 34 yards.
John Harbaugh had long been against Skattebo's flipping — Skattebo notably failed on a backflip over the offseason, months after his rookie year ended with a serious ankle injury (not suffered on a flip). He was pleased to hear about Skattebo's intention not to backflip earlier in the week. "I support his decision, and I hope he scores a lot of touchdowns," Harbaugh said. "I hope he gets an opportunity to prove it real soon. That'd be great."After Skattebo reneged, Harbaugh didn't exactly look pleased on the sideline.
After the game, though, Skattebo explained that the charged atmosphere and the significance of the first down played huge roles.
"When energy calls for it, it calls for it," Skattebo said. "My teammates, I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul. So when that happens, it's second nature, and it's hard to hold back from."
Harbaugh, meanwhile, offered a bit of a wry/forced/half smile and said, "Yeah, he couldn't help himself, could he? Just couldn't help himself."
For now, though, Harbaugh will at least be relieved Skattebo made up for his mistake with a big run and didn't get hurt celebrating. Only time will tell if this was a one-off or if the backflip celebration — like Skattebo on that crucial play — cannot be contained.

title: What's next for the Mets after record-breaking deal with Tarik Skubal? Biggest needs for 2027 - CBS Sports
description: Even after inserting the two-time Cy Young winner at the front of the rotation, the Mets still need pitching help
body:
Even after inserting the two-time Cy Young winner at the front of the rotation, the Mets still need pitching help and more
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Mets landed the offseason's best free agent and one of the game's top pitchers Sunday evening. The Mets and two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal have agreed to a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. The contract obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee (Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million) and average annual value (Max Scherzer's and Justin Verlander's $43.3 million). A 1-of-1 contract for a 1-of-1 pitcher.      New York's offseason work is not complete, however. It's not close to complete, really. The Mets went 74-88 and disappointed every which way this past season. There are still roster needs to address. Here's what's left for the Mets to do this offseason following the Skubal signing.      1. Add another starting pitcher      Yes, the Mets still need another starter even after signing Skubal. They have an excellent 1-2-3 punch. The depth behind that top three is not great, however. Here is New York's updated rotation depth chart:      LHP Tarik SkubalRHP Nolan McLeanRHP Christian ScottLHP Zac ThorntonLHP Sean ManaeaRHP Kodai SengaRHP Tylor Megill (returning from UCL surgery)RHP Jonah TongRHP Justin HagenmanManaea and Senga both pitched so poorly this past season that they were demoted to the bullpen. They shouldn't be counted on as anything more than emergency options at this point in their careers. Thornton had some moments this summer and Tong is not too far removed from being a top prospect, but yeah, the Mets need another starter. Clearly.      
After landing Skubal, I suspect the Mets will aim lower than the second tier of free agent starters (Michael King, Freddy Peralta, Trevor Rogers, etc.) to fill out their rotation. A Clay Holmes reunion would make some sense. Others in that class of veterans make sense too. Think Kevin Gausman, Shota Imanaga, Casey Mize, pitchers like that.      2. Bring in a first baseman      Year 1 post-Pete Alonso at first base went worse than anyone could have expected. Jorge Polanco barely played and was terrible when he did play. Jared Young was fine and owner Steve Cohen isn't running near-record payrolls for fine. Alonso led all first basemen with 5.0 WAR for the Orioles. The Mets finished dead last at the position with -0.8 WAR. Yeesh.      Here are the best available free agent first basemen by FanGraphs projected 2027 WAR:      
Alec Bohm: 2.2 WARTy France: 1.4 WARJosh Bell: 0.9 WARNate Lowe: 0.8 WARPaul Goldschmidt: 0.4 WARIt ain't great. I think the projections on France, who had an excellent season in 2026, are a bit low, but the fact of the matter is he's only had one year in line with the kind of contract he's likely to sign. Perhaps there's a Luis García Jr. trade to be made with the crosstown rival New York Yankees? García's a clunky fit for the Yankees and might be most useful as a trade chip.     The good news is it won't be hard for the Mets to improve at first base. Getting even an average first baseman would represent an enormous upgrade. Now the Mets just have to go out and find that average (or, preferably, better than average) first baseman and improve their lineup. This might be the single biggest item remaining on their offseason to-do list.      3. Keep adding to the bullpenThe Mets traded away several relievers at the deadline this summer (A.J. Minter, Brooks Raley, Luke Weaver, etc.), which allowed them to audition a few young pitchers down the stretch. Left-hander Nate Lavender in particular stood out and cemented his place in the 2027 bullpen. The bullpen pecking order currently looks something like this:      
Closer: RHP Devin WilliamsSetup: LHP Nate Lavender and RHP Dedniel NúñezMiddle: LHP Darwinzon Hernández and RHP Austin WarrenLong: RHP Tobias MyersDepth: RHP Daniel Duarte, RHP Reed Garrett, LHP Cionel Pérez, LHP Jefry YanWilliams was at best inconsistent during his first season with the Mets. Another late-inning reliever to share the high-leverage load (someone to replace Weaver, basically) seems essential. You don't want to pay Skubal all that money only to have the bullpen blow his starts, you know? President of baseball operations David Stearns is adept at building bullpens on the cheap. Spending money is OK too.      Assuming the Mets don't go to the top of the market for Adrian Morejon, the best available free agent relievers are battle-tested veterans like Bryan Abreu, JoJo Romero, and Alex Vesia. Abreu is an excellent buy-low candidate after his rocky first half. There is no such thing as too many good relievers. The Mets should continue adding to their bullpen this winter.      4. More extensions      The case can be made that Skubal's contract is only the second smartest contract the Mets gave out this weekend. They agreed to an eight-year, $95 million contract with a ninth-year club option with center fielder A.J. Ewing on Saturday. The deal buys out his six years of team control and two free agent years with an option for a third. That's a nifty piece of business.      
I would expect the Mets to pursue extensions with McLean and outfielder Carson Benge next, if they haven't already. McLean and Benge both had terrific first full seasons in the big leagues and look like keepers, like players who can be centerpieces for a World Series contender rather than just tag along for the ride. Locking up McLean and/or Benge would be fantastic work.
